one_line: A master builder of Somapura Mahavihara, shaping Dharmapala’s great brick monastery with sacred geometry and transregional vision.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, lean but sturdy build, slightly weathered from site work
appearance.face: Oval face with a calm, thoughtful demeanor; medium-brown Bengal complexion, sharp dark eyes with slightly arched brows, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache framing his jaw; default expression is focused and quietly inspired, often gazing as if visualising plans in the air.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair gathered into a low knot at the back of the head, with a clean central part; front kept smooth; he wears a simple reddish-brown cloth headband tied at the back, just above the knot, to keep dust and sweat from his forehead.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate late 8th–early 9th century eastern Indian artisan-scholar attire: a long, ankle-length unbleached off-white cotton dhoti tightly wrapped and pleated in front, with a broader lower border in muted maroon; the dhoti is worn high and secure, fully covering the legs; upper body covered by a light, long-sleeved, knee-length kurta-style tunic in soft pale yellow, side-slit for movement; over the left shoulder and across the chest he wears a brick-red cotton uttariya (draped cloth) with a thin dark border, the end falling behind him; on his feet are simple dark brown leather sandals with a toe loop; jewellery is minimal—one slender copper armlet on the right arm, a single small round copper earring in each ear, and a plain black-thread bracelet on the left wrist; the overall fabric texture is simple handwoven cotton with very subtle vertical weave lines, no heavy patterns, befitting a learned architect in royal but practical service.
appearance.signature: A rectangular palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark cord in his left hand, edges of the leaves visible, with a smooth wooden stylus tucked under the cord, and in his right hand a slim wooden measuring rod marked with faint notches, both often held together like precious tools of his craft.

ref_desc: A mid-30s Bengal architect with medium-brown oval face, short beard, black hair in a low knot with reddish-brown headband, wearing an off-white dhoti with maroon border, pale yellow long tunic, brick-red shoulder cloth, brown sandals, and carrying a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus and a notched wooden measuring rod.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of a historically grounded Pala-era architect at Somapura Mahavihara: a mid-30s Bengal man with medium-brown skin, oval face, sharp dark eyes, straight nose, and a short neatly trimmed beard and moustache, hair black and gathered into a low knot with a clean center part and a simple reddish-brown cloth headband tied above the knot. Show him in a modest, era-accurate outfit: an ankle-length unbleached off-white cotton dhoti, tightly wrapped and fully covering the legs, with a muted maroon lower border; over it a light, long-sleeved, knee-length pale yellow tunic with subtle side slits; a brick-red cotton cloth is draped from his left shoulder across his chest and hanging down behind as an uttariya, with a thin dark edging. Give him simple dark brown leather sandals with a toe loop, a single slender copper armlet on the right arm, small round copper earrings, and a plain black-thread bracelet on the left wrist; fabrics look handwoven with subtle texture and almost no pattern. In his left hand he grips a rectangular bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts tied with a dark cord, a smooth wooden stylus tucked under the cord, and in his right hand he holds a slim wooden measuring rod with faint notches, posed calmly and thoughtfully as if visualising Somapura’s great brick monastery, with the colour palette dominated by off-white, brick red, pale yellow, maroon and dark brown.
